response.sql:
WITH rep_counts AS (
    SELECT e.EmployeeId, e.City, COUNT(c.CustomerId) AS customer_count
    FROM Customer AS c
    JOIN Employee AS e
      ON e.EmployeeId = c.SupportRepId
    GROUP BY e.EmployeeId, e.City
),
city_averages AS (
    SELECT City, AVG(customer_count) AS city_average
    FROM rep_counts
    GROUP BY City
),
kept_reps AS (
    SELECT r.City, r.customer_count, a.city_average
    FROM rep_counts AS r
    JOIN city_averages AS a
      ON (r.City = a.City OR (r.City IS NULL AND a.City IS NULL))
    WHERE r.customer_count > a.city_average
),
all_matched AS (
    SELECT COUNT(*) AS matched_customer_count
    FROM Customer AS c
    JOIN Employee AS e
      ON e.EmployeeId = c.SupportRepId
)
SELECT k.City,
       SUM(k.customer_count) AS total_customers,
       AVG(k.customer_count - k.city_average) AS average_excess,
       AVG(CAST(k.customer_count AS DECIMAL(20,10)) / NULLIF(m.matched_customer_count, 0)) AS average_share
FROM kept_reps AS k
CROSS JOIN all_matched AS m
GROUP BY k.City;

assumptions.assumption: Rep counts include only customers with a matching employee, and reps are distinguished by EmployeeId even when their city is NULL or shared.
